name: Loma del Pliegue Tumbado
region: Los Glaciares National Park, north sector
why: The one viewpoint with Fitz Roy and Cerro Torre side by side, and Lago Viedma behind you.
book: Free, no permit. It starts at the park visitor centre at the entrance of the village.
water: Only in the forest at the start: carry 2 litres.
dangers: The top is a bare ridge with no shelter: the wind is the strongest of any El Chaltén trail.
Only worth it on a clear day.
turnaround: If the summit is in cloud at the edge of the forest, turn back: the view is the whole point.

points.name: Los Glaciares visitor centre, El Chaltén
points.note: Start behind the ranger station; the path climbs through lenga forest from the first minute.

points.name: Pliegue Tumbado ridge, above the forest
points.note: The trees end: Laguna Toro and the Southern Ice Field appear to the west.

points.name: Loma del Pliegue Tumbado
points.note: About 1,500 m. Fitz Roy to the right, Cerro Torre to the left, Lago Viedma behind.
